sentences.text: Der Herbst beginnt in Deutschland.
sentences.translation: Autumn is beginning in Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: Same pattern as 'Der Sommer beginnt' — subject + verb + location. 'der Herbst' (autumn) is masculine.

sentences.text: Die Blätter werden bunt und fallen von den Bäumen.
sentences.translation: The leaves turn colorful and fall from the trees.
sentences.grammarNote: 'werden' + adjective = to become/turn: 'werden bunt' = turn colorful. 'von + Dativ' shows origin: 'von den Bäumen' = from the trees.

sentences.text: Die Temperaturen fallen langsam.
sentences.translation: Temperatures are slowly falling.
sentences.grammarNote: 'fallen' (to fall) is a strong verb but regular in the plural Präsens: sie fallen. 'langsam' (slowly) has the same form as the adjective.

sentences.text: Viele Menschen tragen jetzt eine warme Jacke.
sentences.translation: Many people now wear a warm jacket.
sentences.grammarNote: 'tragen' is a strong verb: du/er/sie/es trägt, but wir/sie tragen (no change in plural). 'eine warme Jacke' is Akkusativ, weak ending after 'eine'.

sentences.text: Der Herbst ist für viele die schönste Jahreszeit.
sentences.translation: Autumn is, for many, the most beautiful season.
sentences.grammarNote: Superlative with 'der/die/das + -ste': 'die schönste' = the most beautiful. 'für viele' = for many (people), Akkusativ after 'für'.

words.grammar: schön → schönste · Superlativ · Nominativ · Singular · Femininum

articles.title: Das Oktoberfest in München lockt Millionen Besucher

sentences.text: Das Oktoberfest in München hat begonnen.
sentences.translation: The Oktoberfest in Munich has begun.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt tense: 'hat' + past participle 'begonnen' at the end. 'beginnen' is a strong verb with an irregular past participle.

words.grammar: beginnen · Perfekt · hat + begonnen · unregelmäßiges Partizip II

sentences.text: Millionen Besucher kommen jedes Jahr nach München.
sentences.translation: Millions of visitors come to Munich every year.
sentences.grammarNote: 'nach + Stadt' = to a city (direction). 'Millionen Besucher' needs no article or linking word before the noun, like other numbers.

words.grammar: der Besucher · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural
nach · mit Dativ · Richtung zu Städten

sentences.text: Die Besucher trinken Bier und essen Brezeln.
sentences.translation: The visitors drink beer and eat pretzels.
sentences.grammarNote: Two verbs joined by 'und' — no change in word order since 'und' is a coordinating conjunction. 'Bier' and 'Brezeln' are direct objects (Akkusativ) with no article.

sentences.text: Viele Besucher tragen traditionelle Kleidung.
sentences.translation: Many visitors wear traditional clothing.
sentences.grammarNote: 'traditionelle Kleidung' is Akkusativ, strong plural ending since there's no article before 'traditionelle'; 'Kleidung' is uncountable and used generally here.

sentences.text: Das Fest dauert bis Anfang Oktober.
sentences.translation: The festival lasts until early October.
sentences.grammarNote: 'bis + time expression' = until. 'Anfang Oktober' (early October) is a fixed time phrase with no preposition needed before the month.

words.grammar: der Anfang · used adverbially before month names: Anfang Oktober

sentences.text: Jedes Jahr findet der Berlin-Marathon statt.
sentences.translation: Every year, the Berlin Marathon takes place.
sentences.grammarNote: Separable verb 'stattfinden': the prefix 'statt' goes to the end of the clause. 'Jedes Jahr' at the start triggers inversion.

sentences.text: Über vierzigtausend Läufer nehmen teil.
sentences.translation: Over forty thousand runners take part.
sentences.grammarNote: 'über' here means 'more than', not location. 'teilnehmen' is separable: 'teil' goes to the end of the clause.

words.grammar: der Läufer · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural

sentences.text: Die Strecke führt durch die ganze Stadt.
sentences.translation: The route leads through the whole city.
sentences.grammarNote: 'durch + Akkusativ' = through (movement across). 'die ganze Stadt' = the whole city, 'ganze' takes a weak ending after 'die'.

sentences.text: Viele Zuschauer stehen am Straßenrand und jubeln.
sentences.translation: Many spectators stand at the roadside and cheer.
sentences.grammarNote: 'am Straßenrand' = 'an dem Straßenrand', contracted, Dativ for location. 'jubeln' (to cheer) is a regular weak verb.

words.grammar: der Zuschauer · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural

sentences.text: Der Sieger läuft die Strecke in etwas mehr als zwei Stunden.
sentences.translation: The winner runs the route in just over two hours.
sentences.grammarNote: 'in + Dativ' for a time duration: 'in zwei Stunden' = in two hours. 'etwas mehr als' = a little more than, a fixed comparison phrase.

sentences.text: Immer mehr Deutsche kaufen ein Elektroauto.
sentences.translation: More and more Germans are buying an electric car.
sentences.grammarNote: 'immer mehr' = more and more, a fixed intensifying phrase. 'ein Elektroauto' is Akkusativ, direct object of 'kaufen'.

sentences.text: Die Verkäufe sind in diesem Jahr stark gestiegen.
sentences.translation: Sales have risen sharply this year.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt with 'sein' (not 'haben') because 'steigen' describes a change of state. 'stark' modifies 'gestiegen' like an adverb.

sentences.text: Ein Elektroauto braucht keine Tankstelle.
sentences.translation: An electric car doesn't need a gas station.
sentences.grammarNote: 'keine' negates the indefinite article before a feminine noun: 'keine Tankstelle' = no gas station.

sentences.text: Die Regierung unterstützt den Kauf mit Geld.
sentences.translation: The government supports the purchase with money.
sentences.grammarNote: 'mit + Dativ' = with (a means). 'den Kauf' is Akkusativ, the direct object of 'unterstützt'.

sentences.text: Experten erwarten noch mehr Elektroautos auf den Straßen.
sentences.translation: Experts expect even more electric cars on the roads.
sentences.grammarNote: 'noch mehr' = even more, intensifying 'mehr'. 'auf + Dativ' for location: 'auf den Straßen' = on the roads.
